Step 0 is ruling 18; the Cottonwood slice is built under all three addenda. The channel was BLOCKED on a registry key until 4.0.0_SA_CRO landed MASTER z09 -> cottonwood @de56cfd02f on 1.0.0_SA_CTO ruling 102723 (CRO 102727, CTO 102729, GO 102730).

artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: Commits bf1683f172 (ruling 18) then e79dd684bf (the Cottonwood rules). RULING 18: a sixth status FOLLOWS-DISCONTINUITY, applied to a row that would otherwise read OK when the account's previous trading day was IMPLAUSIBLE-RETURN. It does NOT cascade (only an IMPLAUSIBLE-RETURN day triggers it) and never overwrites a row already carrying its own named reason. The mechanism is ImplausibleIndex, a memoised (source, day) -> accounts lookup -- the only rule in this producer that reaches across days. Recursion terminates because _frame_for() grades ruling 16 only, so asking for D-1's implausible set cannot ask for D-2's, and the memo is what keeps the cost off 2x (49F: 1,832 cache hits against 1,508 misses). THE COTTONWOOD RULES: price_of() reads a declared price_column when there is one and otherwise derives value/quantity, selected STRUCTURALLY so it is a declaration shape and never a firm branch; an absent OR ZERO quantity yields a NULL price (ruling 4's price-missing). _flag() parses a boolean column however the silver stored it and REFUSES an unparseable value. validate_entry() now requires one of price_column or quantity_column.

The THIRD channel, added as an entry and never a code branch (ruling 1). Keyed `blackdiamond_z09`, declaring registry_key z09, monolith blackdiamond, the templated prefix {monolith}/{scope}/silver/fact_holdings/, account_id_zero_pad 0, identifier_columns [CUSIP, Symbol, Asset Name], value_column `Market Value`, quantity_column `Units`, price_column NULL (the channel publishes no price) and cash_flag_column `Cash Equivalent`. NO FIRM TOKEN IS TYPED: naming-gate on the entry's diff reads PASS, 1 graded (opal-data-assets, CONFORMANT as S3_BUCKET), 0 REFUSE. Every measured claim carries its denominator, and one of them was CORRECTED during verification: the first draft said the 6,775 price-missing rows carry -7,607,341.30 in Market Value. They carry EXACTLY 0.00. That figure is the 31 NEGATIVE-Units rows, which are priced (a short's value and units are both negative, so the derived price is positive and correct) and which ruling 15 then puts outside the basket. The declaration now says so.

Commits bf1683f172 then e79dd684bf. 45 passed (was 39 at round 3). Ruling 18: the glitch-then-reversion pair the ruling was written for -- a price 100 -> 250 -> 100 reads +150% then -60%, and the REVERSION is an ORDINARY day on its own arithmetic, which is exactly why it needed a rule rather than a wider ruling-16 band; plus the no-cascade and no-overwrite bounds, both of which a looser reading would cross. The Cottonwood rules: Market Value / Units gives the same +10% a published price would, and a UNIT change with the value is NOT a price move (2,200 over 20 units is still 110.00); absent AND zero Units are both price-missing with the account_value left finite; the text cash flag is parsed and an unparseable value REFUSES. The status-vocabulary test caught the sixth member on its own, which is what it is for.

mutant.description: TWO planted mutants on the two Cottonwood claims, each written through the producer's own path and each restored by re-running the producer for that day rather than by writing the good bytes back. M1 attacks E4-AC1's 'every account has exactly one row': account z0925724581 was dropped from the landed date=2026-09-25 daily partition. M2 attacks E4-AC2's coverage claim: the whole date=2026-08-12 daily partition was deleted -- a MID-HISTORY day, not an endpoint, because an endpoint is the one a range check is most likely to notice for the wrong reason.
mutant.expected: M1 -> E4-AC1 FAIL naming 1 missing account, then PASS at 0 after the restore. M2 -> E4-AC2 FAIL naming 1 missing gold partition and printing the date, then PASS at 0 after the restore.
mutant.observed: M1 PLANTED: 'gold rows at 2026-09-25: 983 | missing 1' / E4-AC1 FAIL. M1 RESTORED: 'gold rows 984 | missing 0' / E4-AC1 PASS. M2 PLANTED: 'computable 75 | missing gold 1 (first [2026-08-12])' / E4-AC2 FAIL. M2 RESTORED: 'missing gold 0' / E4-AC2 PASS. Both criteria are live oracles and neither passes on absence. NOTE, as at round 3: M1's manifest limb did NOT fire -- with the row dropped straight out of the parquet the manifest still read accounts_with_prior_holdings 984 / complete true, because it is the producer's own SELF-REPORT of the frame it emitted rather than a reading of the bytes that survived. The row-level 'missing 1' limb is what caught it.

determinism.method: Three instruments. (a) date=2026-09-25 was produced three times -- the pre-run dry run, the 75-day upload, and the M1 restore -- and the census compared across all three; date=2026-08-12 twice. (b) The landed row total was read back from the parquet FOOTERS, an instrument the producer does not touch, and compared with its printed tally. (c) THE VALUE DECOMPOSITION was reconciled against the silver independently of both.
determinism.observed: date=2026-09-25 produced 984 rows on every run with the identical census {OK 908, NON-POSITIVE-BASE 62, ALL-HOLDINGS-EXCLUDED 14} and identical counts (984/908/76, complete True). FOOTER vs TALLY: 66,587 = 66,587 over 75 partitions. RECONCILIATION: included 562,744,973.40 + excluded 43,493.21 + negative -7,607,341.30 = 555,181,125.32 against the silver's own 555,181,125.32 over 19,784 rows -- to the cent, and it is what turned a suspected coincidence into a checked identity. 0 tracebacks; 0 days not computed; no day reported complete=False.

declared_exclusions.item: The structural selector that would have avoided the registry row
declared_exclusions.reason: Under blackdiamond, 49financial carries masters and cottonwood carries none, so 'the master-less blackdiamond scope' would have selected it with no token anywhere and the cell would have completed hours earlier. REJECTED: it encodes an accident of the current registry as a firm's identity, which fails CLAUDE.md rule 24 (iii) -- the axis would be 'has masters', not identity -- and rule 30 says a builder refusal IS a missing registry row, never a cleverer predicate. The row landed instead, and it is reusable by every future channel.
